issues.description: The triage note records a sudden onset of the headache, while the provider note describes a gradual onset. Which account is correct, and was the difference noticed?
The discharge summary gives a different coiling date than the procedure note. Which date is correct?

The headache was attributed to migraine without imaging on 2024-03-28, and a subarachnoid hemorrhage was found on CT at the return visit on 2024-04-01. Was neuro-imaging considered at the first visit?

Author: E. Ramanathan, MD
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Triage: headache onset sudden while lifting weights, rated 9/10, per patient report.

Date of service: 03-28-24. Patient presents with headache.

HPI: headache of gradual onset over several hours with photophobia and nausea.

PMH: mild intermittent asthma, GERD. PSH: none reported. Allergies: no known drug
allergies. Social: former smoker, quit over ten years ago. Lives with family.

Vitals: BP 122/76, HR 90, RR 18, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 36.9 C.

Neuro exam: alert and oriented, cranial nerves intact, no focal deficit.

Given metoclopramide 10 mg IV and diphenhydramine 25 mg IV with partial relief.

Impression: migraine without aura. No imaging obtained at this visit.

Return precautions for worsening headache, fever or neck stiffness. Follow up with primary
care within one week.

I personally evaluated the patient and reviewed the available records. Documentation
completed with the assistance of templated text and reviewed for accuracy.
